back: Alumina dissolved in molten cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) at about 950 °C.
Cathode: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al. Anode: 2O²⁻ → O₂ + 4e⁻, then C + O₂ → CO₂.
Hot oxygen produced at the anode burns the carbon to carbon dioxide.
Brine: Cl₂ at the titanium anode, H₂ and OH⁻ at the nickel cathode; the membrane passes Na⁺ only, giving NaOH and keeping products apart.
Water treatment, PVC, bleach, hydrochloric acid.
Soap and detergents, paper, purifying bauxite, textiles.

front: Electrolytic refining of copper or nickel
back: Impure anode dissolves; pure metal deposits on the cathode; less reactive metals form anode sludge; more reactive ones stay in solution.

front: Main economic factor in industrial electrolysis
back: Electricity cost: plants are sited near cheap power; recycling saves energy.
